title: Worksheet — Quadratic Equations (Class 10 NIOS Mathematics)
instructions: Attempt all 10 questions in your notebook. Show every step of your working for the subjective questions; choose the single best option for MCQs. Answers without working will not receive full marks. Total time: 50 minutes.

questions.question: Which of the following is in the standard form of a quadratic equation?
questions.explanation: Standard form is a x^2 + b x + c = 0 with a ≠ 0. Only the third option matches.

questions.question: Every quadratic equation a x^2 + b x + c = 0 has at most two real roots.
questions.explanation: A polynomial of degree 2 can have at most 2 real roots; a parabola crosses the x-axis at most twice.

questions.question: The discriminant of the quadratic equation a x^2 + b x + c = 0 is D = ____.
questions.explanation: D = b^2 − 4 a c controls the nature of the roots.

questions.question: What is the discriminant of 3 x^2 − 5 x + 2 = 0?
The roots of the equation x^2 − 5 x + 6 = 0 are:
Solve 6 x^2 + x − 15 = 0 by factorisation, showing all steps.
questions.answer: Need two numbers with product 6 × (−15) = −90 and sum 1: the pair (10, −9). 6 x^2 + 10 x − 9 x − 15 = 0 → 2 x (3 x + 5) − 3 (3 x + 5) = 0 → (3 x + 5)(2 x − 3) = 0 → x = −5/3 or x = 3/2.
questions.explanation: Use the split-the-middle-term technique with the pair (10, −9).

questions.question: Solve x^2 − 6 x + 5 = 0 by completing the square.
questions.explanation: Add (b/2)^2 = 9 to both sides to make the LHS a perfect square.

questions.question: Use the quadratic formula to solve 2 x^2 − 7 x + 3 = 0. State the discriminant explicitly.
questions.explanation: Substitute into x = (−b ± √D) / (2a) after computing D.

questions.question: The area of a rectangle is 60 m^2 and its length is 4 m more than its breadth. Find the length and breadth.
questions.answer: Let the breadth be x m. Then the length is (x + 4) m. From x (x + 4) = 60 we get x^2 + 4 x − 60 = 0. Factorise: (x + 10)(x − 6) = 0 → x = −10 or x = 6. Reject x = −10 (negative breadth is impossible). So breadth = 6 m and length = 6 + 4 = 10 m. Check: 6 × 10 = 60 m^2. ✓
questions.explanation: Step 1: name the unknown. Step 2: build the quadratic. Step 3: solve. Step 4: reject the negative root.

questions.question: (a) Derive the quadratic formula by completing the square on a x^2 + b x + c = 0 (a ≠ 0). (b) Use it to discuss the three cases for the nature of the roots in terms of the discriminant D = b^2 − 4 a c.
questions.answer: (a) Divide a x^2 + b x + c = 0 by a: x^2 + (b/a) x + c/a = 0. Move the constant: x^2 + (b/a) x = −c/a. Add (b/(2a))^2 to both sides: x^2 + (b/a) x + (b/(2a))^2 = (b^2 − 4 a c)/(4 a^2). The LHS is a perfect square: (x + b/(2a))^2 = (b^2 − 4 a c)/(4 a^2). Take square roots: x + b/(2a) = ± √(b^2 − 4 a c) / (2a). Hence x = (−b ± √(b^2 − 4 a c)) / (2 a). (b) Set D = b^2 − 4 a c. If D > 0 the formula gives two distinct real values, so the equation has two distinct real roots. If D = 0 the formula gives x = −b / (2 a) twice, so the equation has one repeated real root. If D < 0 the square root is not real, so the equation has no real roots.
questions.explanation: The derivation is exactly the completing-the-square algorithm carried out symbolically; the discriminant arises naturally as the right-hand side after the perfect-square step.
